topStories.headline: Planners Clear Path for Marina Safeway Tower, Opponents Threaten Lawsuit
topStories.dek: San Francisco's Planning Department has ruled the 848-unit Align Real Estate project eligible for state-mandated streamlined approval under AB 2011, marking a major turning point in the neighborhood battle over the 15 Marina Blvd. site.
topStories.body:
San Francisco planners determined this week that the controversial housing tower proposed on the site of the Marina District Safeway meets the eligibility requirements of AB 2011, the 2022 California law that allows qualifying housing projects on commercially zoned sites to bypass much of the local discretionary review process. The decision, which came just before the statutory deadline last Thursday, puts the project on a state-mandated path toward accelerated approval and effectively closes off a central line of attack from neighbors who argued the site did not qualify.

Developer Align Real Estate is proposing to raze the nearly seven-decade-old grocery store at 15 Marina Blvd. and replace it with a new Safeway at street level beneath 848 apartments — including 86 affordable units — in a building rising up to 22 stories. The Planning Department now has 90 days to formally approve or deny the project on a ministerial basis, with far less discretionary review than a conventional development would face.

Opponents, including several neighborhood groups represented by attorney Stuart Gross, have warned of a lawsuit if the city allows the project to proceed without first resolving what they describe as an unresolved environmental testing gap. In an August 11 letter to the directors of the city's Planning and Public Health departments, Gross warned that the groups would sue, citing contamination concerns. Environmental assessments have found petroleum hydrocarbons and other contaminants in soil and groundwater above applicable screening thresholds — a legacy of the site's use by PG&E as a steam power plant before Safeway purchased the property in 1959. State regulators have said the findings do not pose an immediate exposure risk but have called for additional testing before residential redevelopment proceeds.

The project has drawn opposition from across the political spectrum, including Mayor Daniel Lurie and District Supervisor Stephen Sherrill, who represent the area. Opponents have argued the tower is out of character for the low-slung waterfront neighborhood, while supporters contend San Francisco must embrace state housing law to meet its regional housing mandate.

topStories.headline: Marina West Harbor Dredging Complete, But Second Round Planned for Fall
topStories.dek: After months of blocked access that stranded boaters and raised emergency-response concerns, the SF Recreation and Parks Department reports the spring dredging episode at the Marina's West Harbor entrance was completed on June 28, with a follow-up episode now planned for October.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Marina's West Harbor entrance, which had been severely obstructed for months by a sandbar that restricted access for boaters, businesses, nonprofits, and emergency responders, was cleared following a spring dredging campaign. According to the SF Marina Harbor Association, citing SF Recreation and Parks, the spring 2026 dredging episode at the entrance to West Harbor was completed on June 28, 2026, and will be followed by another episode in October.

The months-long obstruction drew sharp criticism from harbor users, who argued the city moved too slowly to address the sand buildup. City officials said the sand had accumulated "more quickly than expected." Harbormaster Scott Grindy has since discussed upcoming dredging in August and September as well as other infrastructure concerns, including damage to the seawall between the St. Francis and Golden Gate Yacht Clubs from winter storms.

According to the SF Recreation and Park Department's harbor webpage, dredging to date has removed 38,710 cubic yards of sediment from the waterway entrance, increasing depth and improving navigation safety. Marina staff continues to publish weekly channel sounding reports on Thursdays, and officials caution boaters to take extra precautions when water levels are low, as sand conditions near the north entrance side continue to shift with tidal movement. Officials are also planning to install a breakwater at the end of the jetty as a longer-term solution to reduce future sand accumulation.

topStories.headline: SF History Association Returns to Pacific Heights for August Talk
topStories.dek: The San Francisco History Association holds its monthly lecture series at Congregation Sherith Israel in Pacific Heights on Tuesday, August 25, open to the public for $10.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco History Association will hold its monthly SF History Night lecture at Newman Hall inside Congregation Sherith Israel, 2266 California Street at Webster in Pacific Heights, on Tuesday, August 25, 2026. Doors open at 7:00 p.m. and the program begins at approximately 7:45 p.m.

The monthly series features local history experts presenting themed talks, usually accompanied by a slide show and light refreshments. Past presentations have covered a wide range of San Francisco history topics, from the Fire Department to Victorian architecture to vintage stories from Playland-at-the-Beach. Admission is $10 for the general public and free for San Francisco History Association members.

Congregation Sherith Israel, which dates to 1851 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, is a storied venue in its own right. Its current building, completed in 1905 and designed by architect Albert Pissis in Beaux-Arts, Byzantine Revival, and Romanesque Revival styles, features a 120-foot dome, hand-carved Honduran mahogany, and hundreds of stained-glass panels. The building served as a courthouse following the 1906 earthquake and fire.

moreNews.headline: Toxic Contamination Claims Add New Front to Marina Safeway Battle
moreNews.body: Even as planners cleared the Align Real Estate project for streamlined review, a parallel fight over environmental safety has escalated. In an August 11 letter to city officials, attorney Stuart Gross warned that 2023 testing found petroleum contamination in soil at concentrations up to 2,500 milligrams per kilogram — described by the state Department of Toxic Substances Control as "about twice the commercial screening level, and ten times the residential screening level." Environmental assessments have also identified petroleum hydrocarbons, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, PCE, and chloroform in soil vapor. Opponents argue an Environmental Impact Report is required before construction can proceed; the city and developer contend that environmental review occurs later, during permitting and construction under the oversight of the health department and the water board.

moreNews.headline: Marina Harbor Faces Another Round of Dredging Infrastructure Questions
moreNews.body: Following the spring 2026 dredging of the West Harbor entrance, harbor officials are planning a second dredging episode for October and have flagged additional infrastructure concerns. Harbormaster Scott Grindy noted extensive damage to the seawall between the St. Francis and Golden Gate Yacht Clubs from winter storms, noting the seawall lacks proper riprap protection. Officials are also addressing sinking pilings in East Harbor with temporary sleeve patches while a longer-term harbor renovation plan — which would include reorienting slips and installing a sheet-pile breakwater — advances through environmental review. The harbor is currently at 88% occupancy.

moreNews.headline: Pacific Heights Condo Market Posts Strong July With Supply at Ten-Year Low
moreNews.body: A new market report shows Pacific Heights condos had a notably active July 2026, with 16 closed sales and three-quarters of them closing above asking price. Months of supply fell to the lowest level in ten years of tracked data, even as the median price dipped — a dynamic the report attributes to a shift in the mix of units sold rather than softening demand. The three-month sales average is up roughly 28% compared to the same period last year, according to data from the San Francisco MLS as of August 14, 2026.

restaurants.name: Causwells
